issues.description: Indentation bug: `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11)` block sits outside the class but the surrounding edit collapsed the blank line separating `Math_unary` and `Math_atan2`, and the version-gated registration sits at module scope where it should be — but only if `Math_unary` is still a class at that point. Verify it parses; the diff shows the trailing blank line of the class body was deleted.
issues.detail: The diff removes the blank line after the `signatures = [...]` list inside `Math_unary` and immediately starts `if sys.version_info >= (3, 11):` at column 0. Python will accept this (the list literal terminates the class body), but it is fragile and reads as if the `if` is part of the class. Restore the blank line so the class body clearly ends before the module-level conditional.

Both files newly reference `sys.version_info` but the diff only adds `import sys` to `numba/core/typing/mathdecl.py`. If `sys` is not already imported in those two modules, this will raise `NameError` at import time on every Python version. Either add the import or, better, use the project's existing `PYVERSION` constant from `numba.core.utils` (already used in the test) for consistency.

issues.description: Version-gate the data, not the code: use the existing `PYVERSION` tuple everywhere
issues.detail: The test file uses `PYVERSION >= (3, 11)` from `numba.core.utils`, but the two impl files and the typing file invent their own `sys.version_info >= (3, 11)` check. Pick one — preferably the project's `PYVERSION` — so the version gate is a single data point referenced from three sites, not three independent string comparisons drifting over time. Data dominates; the version is data.

issues.description: Release note file missing trailing newline
issues.detail: `docs/upcoming_changes/10276.new_feature.rst` ends without a newline (`\ No newline at end of file`). Trivial, but POSIX text files end in `\n`; most linters and `cat`-style filters expect it. One byte fix.

issues.description: Release note underline length and content are perfunctory
issues.detail: The underline `------------------------------` is the same length as the title, which is fine, but the body just restates the title ("Support for ``math.exp2`` is added."). One sentence noting the Python 3.11+ requirement would save a future reader a trip to the source.

The list `[-2, -1, -2, 2, 1, 2, .1, .2]` was copy-pasted from `test_exp` and contains `-2` twice while missing `0`. For `exp2` specifically, `exp2(0) == 1` is a useful boundary. Small data fix; the algorithm (run_unary) is fine.

issues.description: Docs entry should note the Python 3.11+ minimum
issues.detail: `pysupported.rst` lists `math.exp2` alongside `math.exp` with no qualifier, but the implementation is conditional on Python >= 3.11. A short parenthetical ("(Python 3.11+)") would prevent a 3.10 user from filing a bug. The data structure here is the supported-functions list; annotate the row, don't hide the version constraint in source.

review.summary: The change is the right shape — `math.exp2` maps cleanly onto the existing `unary_math_intr(... 'llvm.exp2')` filter, so the new function composes with the existing data-driven registration pattern. SMALL-AND-COMPOSABLE on the core mechanism. The problems are all at the seams: `sys` is referenced in two files that don't appear to import it; the version gate is reinvented three times instead of pulling the project's existing `PYVERSION` constant; a class-body blank line was removed making the conditional registration read ambiguously; and the docs/test data has small copy-paste artifacts (duplicate `-2`, missing newline, no version note). Fix the import and unify on `PYVERSION` before merge; the rest are nits.
